properties.description:
Twelve tests.

Unit, in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/file_handles.rs (6): flo2.io's numbers (64 designs, cap 64, soft 1024 / hard 524288) need 64 × 76 + 32 = 4896 and the warning names every number, 'ulimit -n 4896', '--ulimit nofile=4896:4896' and 'lower --registry-max-open to 13 or fewer'; after the raise (524288) and at exactly 4896 nothing is said, at 4895 it is; a hard limit too low names who can raise it; a limit below one design says 0 rather than underflowing; the headroom line says unknown rather than guessing and carries no path; on Linux the count includes files this process holds.

Unit, in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/readiness.rs (2 new): /readyz keeps its status and first line, adds 'open files: 1013 of 1024 allowed (11 left)' and the headers x-reflow2-open-files / x-reflow2-open-file-limit (unknown, unlimited); on Linux the count is real and under the limit.

End-to-end over the real binary, crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_registry_checks_its_file_handles_at_start.rs (2, Unix): soft 200 / hard 256 with 8 designs logs the raise to 256, warns 640 against 256 and keeps answering /readyz 200 with the headroom; soft 100 / hard 1024 with 2 designs raises and says nothing.
properties.findings: All pass on Linux (ajs77, Rust 1.99.0, --no-default-features): 10 lib tests (file_handles + readiness) and the 2 end-to-end tests in the in_memory program. Also run by hand on the dev binary: under soft=hard=1024 with --registry-max-open 64 it prints the warning (4896 against 1024, lower to 13) and /readyz answers 'open files: 11 of 1024 allowed (1013 left)'; under soft 1024 / hard 524288 (flo2.io's container) it logs 'raised this server's open-file limit from 1024 to 524288' and no warning. cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings (both crates, no RocksDB) clean. CI's full job (RocksDB, macOS not covered) runs the rest on the PR.
properties.name: A registry raises its open-file limit, warns with the three numbers when its designs may not fit, keeps serving, and /readyz reports the headroom
